cards.text: Baker, these are the words of Amos, one of the sheepherders of Tekoa, and what he saw concerns Israel. He saw it two years before the earthquake, when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel. A sheepherder from Tekoa, and I'm a cookie stamper who got called out of a junk drawer, so friend, these eyebrows are staying DOWN.

cards.question: Amos says the LORD roars from Zion and raises His voice from Jerusalem. True or false: Amos then says the pastures of the shepherds rejoice.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks, and He starts with Damascus, the head of Aram (Isaiah 7:8): "For three transgressions of Damascus, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they threshed Gilead with sledges of iron."
So He will send fire upon the house of Hazael to consume the citadels of Ben-hadad. Hazael and Ben-hadad were kings of Aram (2 Kings 13:3).

cards.question: The LORD says He will break down the gates of Damascus. What does He say will happen to the rulers in the Valley of Aven and Beth-eden?
The LORD is judging Damascus, in the land of Aram. True or false: He says the people of Aram will get to stay in their land.

cards.text: Next up is Gaza, a Philistine city (Joshua 13:3), and there's that line again: three transgressions, even four, and no taking back the judgment. That's two nations, friend, and I'm already counting on my mustache.

cards.question: The LORD gives His charge against Gaza. What does He say Gaza did to a whole population?

answers.text: Exiled them and handed them to Edom
Stole all their flocks and herds
Burned their homes to the ground

cards.text: So the LORD will send fire upon the walls of Gaza to consume its citadels. He will cut off the rulers of Ashdod and Ashkelon and turn His hand against Ekron, all Philistine cities too.

cards.question: After Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron, the LORD speaks of the rest of the Philistines. True or false: He says the remnant of the Philistines will perish.

cards.text: Next is Tyre, a fortified city (Joshua 19:29), and the LORD's charge is that Tyre delivered up a whole congregation of exiles to Edom.

cards.question: Tyre handed a whole congregation of exiles over to Edom. Which nation earlier in this list did something like that?
Besides handing exiles over to Edom, what else does the LORD charge Tyre with?

cards.text: So the LORD will send fire upon the walls of Tyre to consume its citadels. Three nations in, and nobody's walked away clean.

Next on the list is Edom, and Esau, Jacob's twin brother, is the father of the Edomites (Genesis 25:24-26; 36:9). The LORD's charge: Edom pursued his brother with the sword and stifled all compassion.

cards.question: Edom stifled all compassion. True or false: the LORD says Edom's anger flared up once and then cooled off.

cards.text: So the LORD will send fire upon Teman to consume the citadels of Bozrah, two places in Edom (Jeremiah 49:7, 13).
Then come the Ammonites, descended from Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 12:5; 19:36, 38). Their charge is heavy: they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead.

cards.question: The Ammonites ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead. What does the LORD say they did it for?

cards.text: So the LORD will kindle a fire in the walls of Rabbah, the Ammonite city (2 Samuel 12:26), to consume its citadels amid war cries on the day of battle and a violent wind on the day of tempest.

cards.question: Rabbah, the Ammonite city, is burning amid war cries. What does the LORD say will happen to the Ammonite king?

answers.text: He will go into exile with his princes
He will flee alone to the desert
He will surrender and keep his throne

cards.text: Next up is Moab, also descended from Lot (Genesis 19:36-37). Five nations down, and friend, I am on the very edge of my gold base waiting on this next charge.

cards.question: Moab burned to lime the bones of Edom's king, another nation's ruler. True or false: the LORD holds Moab responsible for it.

The LORD will send fire against Moab to consume the citadels of Kerioth, and Moab will die in tumult amid war cries and the sound of the ram's horn. True or false: He says only the ruler of Moab will be cut off and his officials will be spared.

cards.text: And now the list comes home: the next name is Judah, where Amos's own town of Tekoa sits (2 Chronicles 11:5-6). It's like nodding along while everybody else's name gets read off a list, and then you hear YOUR name.

cards.question: The LORD's charge against Judah is that they reject the ___ of the LORD and fail to keep His statutes.
Judah is led astray by the lies their fathers walked in. What does that say about Judah's problem?

cards.text: So Judah gets the same fire as the nations before it: fire upon Judah to consume the citadels of Jerusalem. Not one name on this list gets a pass, friend.
